| antigen-escape | Loss of the target antigen or of antigen presentation as an immune-evasion mechanism: antigen-negative relapse (CD19-negative 9–33%), and MHC-I / β2-microglobulin loss (B2M altered in ~29% of melanoma, HLA loss-of-heterozygosity in ~40% of NSCLC) — defeating a working immune or CAR-T response over time | tme-barriers/antigen-escape.md | antigen escape, antigen loss, CD19-negative relapse, BCMA loss, B2M, beta-2-microglobulin, MHC-I, HLA loss of heterozygosity, immune evasion, resistance |
| chemokine-axis-mismatch | The failure of a tumor to produce the CXCR3-ligand chemokines (CXCL9/CXCL10/CXCL11) plus constitutive CCL5 that recruit effector CD8 T cells — via epigenetic silencing (EZH2/H3K27me3, DNMT methylation) or peroxynitrite nitration — so the tumor presents no gradient for effector T cells to follow and instead recruits suppressive myeloid cells | tme-barriers/chemokine-axis-mismatch.md | chemokine, CXCR3, CXCL9, CXCL10, CXCL11, CCL5, CCL2 nitration, EZH2, DNMT, H3K27me3, T-cell recruitment, immune exclusion |
| desmoplastic-stroma-barrier | The dense desmoplastic stroma — cancer-associated fibroblasts, fibrillar collagen, and hyaluronan occupying >80% of tumor volume in pancreatic cancer — that physically excludes T cells and nanoparticles from the tumor parenchyma and generates the solid stress and interstitial hypertension underlying the delivery wall | tme-barriers/desmoplastic-stroma-barrier.md | desmoplasia, stroma, extracellular matrix, cancer-associated fibroblast, CAF, collagen, hyaluronan, FAP, physical exclusion, pancreatic cancer, ECM stiffness |
| interstitial-fluid-pressure | Elevated interstitial fluid pressure inside solid tumors (4–50 mmHg, mean ~20, versus ~0–2 mmHg in normal tissue) that collapses the transvascular pressure gradient and produces an outward convective flow opposing the inward transport of drugs, nanoparticles, and cells — a primary physical reason the EPR effect fails in human tumors | tme-barriers/interstitial-fluid-pressure.md | interstitial fluid pressure, IFP, convective flow, EPR effect, nanoparticle delivery, transvascular gradient, mmHg, tumor perfusion, delivery wall |
| metabolic-hostility | The metabolically hostile solid-tumor milieu that disables T cells: glucose stolen by tumor glycolysis, lactate accumulated to ~50 mM with extracellular pH driven to 6.4–6.8, adenosine generated by the CD39/CD73 axis, and tryptophan (IDO) and arginine (arginase) depleted — each independently crippling T-cell function | tme-barriers/metabolic-hostility.md | metabolic hostility, glucose competition, lactate, acidosis, pH, adenosine, CD39, CD73, tryptophan, IDO, kynurenine, arginine, arginase |
| solid-tumor-immune-response | The stage of mounting an effective, sustained cytotoxic immune attack inside a solid tumor — a two-gate stage where effector T cells must first infiltrate (past chemokine, endothelial, stromal, and pressure barriers) and then function (against immunosuppression, metabolic hostility, and exhaustion) before antigen escape erodes the response | tme-barriers/solid-tumor-immune-response.md | solid tumor immune response, T-cell infiltration, effector function, immune exclusion, two-gate failure, cold tumor, TME barrier, CAR-T solid tumor, binding constraint |
| stroma-modification | Enzymatic or signaling strategies to dismantle the desmoplastic stroma (hyaluronidase, sonic-hedgehog/FAK/LOXL2 inhibition, TGF-β blockade, angiotensin inhibition) to improve delivery and immune access — a largely failed clinical program: PEGPH20 gave no survival benefit in phase 3 and stromal depletion can accelerate tumor aggressiveness | tme-barriers/stroma-modification.md | stroma modification, hyaluronidase, PEGPH20, HALO-301, sonic hedgehog, FAK, LOXL2, TGF-beta, losartan, phase 3 failure, double-edged |
| t-cell-exhaustion | The progressive cell-intrinsic dysfunction of chronically stimulated T cells — imprinted epigenetically by TOX, with terminal cells co-expressing PD-1/TIM-3/LAG-3/TIGIT and losing effector function — a stable state that checkpoint blockade only transiently reinvigorates, so durable control depends on the TCF-1+ progenitor pool that solid-tumor TMEs deplete | tme-barriers/t-cell-exhaustion.md | T-cell exhaustion, TOX, TCF-1, progenitor exhausted, terminal exhausted, PD-1, TIM-3, LAG-3, TIGIT, epigenetic, CAR-T, checkpoint blockade |
| tme-immunosuppression | The suppressive cell populations inside a solid tumor — regulatory T cells (often >50% of tumor T cells), myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and M2 tumor-associated macrophages — that actively neutralize effector T cells through arginase, iNOS/NO, peroxynitrite, IL-10, TGF-β, and adenosine | tme-barriers/tme-immunosuppression.md | immunosuppression, regulatory T cell, Treg, FoxP3, MDSC, arginase, iNOS, tumor-associated macrophage, TAM, M2, CD163, TGF-beta, IL-10 |
| tumor-endothelial-barrier | The tumor vasculature as a selective immune barrier: anergic endothelium that fails to upregulate ICAM-1/VCAM-1 (blocking T-cell extravasation), plus a FasL death barrier and endothelin-B-receptor signaling that selectively kill or exclude effector CD8 T cells while sparing Tregs | tme-barriers/tumor-endothelial-barrier.md | endothelial anergy, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, FasL, endothelin-B receptor, ETBR, extravasation, Treg, c-FLIP, tumor vasculature, T-cell exclusion |
| tumor-hypoxia | Low tumor oxygenation (median pO2 below 2%, roughly ≤10 mmHg, versus 40–65 mmHg in normal tissue) from abnormal vasculature — stabilizing HIF-1α, upregulating CD39/CD73→adenosine and PD-L1, impairing T/NK function, and conferring ~3× radioresistance | tme-barriers/tumor-hypoxia.md | hypoxia, HIF-1alpha, pO2, oxygen, CD39, CD73, adenosine, A2A receptor, PD-L1, radioresistance, immune exclusion |
| vascular-normalization | Restoring tumor-vessel function with judicious anti-VEGF/VEGFR2 dosing — improving perfusion, oxygenation, and adhesion-molecule expression so T cells can extravasate — and, at its most effective, inducing high endothelial venules (HEVs) via LTβR signaling that enrich intratumoral lymphocytes 3–10 fold | tme-barriers/vascular-normalization-hev.md | vascular normalization, anti-VEGF, VEGFR2, high endothelial venule, HEV, LTβR, MECA-79, perfusion, oxygenation, CAR-T delivery, bevacizumab |
